name_en: Hinona — Shiga's slender purple-topped turnip pickled to a cherry pink
summary_ja: 滋賀県日野町で生まれたと伝わる細長いかぶ。地上に出る上部が赤紫、土の中の下部が白く、辛味とほろ苦さがある。塩や酢で漬けると全体が淡い桜色に染まり、日野菜漬けとして近江の冬を彩るとされる。
summary_en: A slender turnip said to have originated in Hino, Shiga. The part that rises above the soil turns red-purple while the buried part stays white, with a sharp, faintly bitter bite. Salted or pickled in vinegar, the whole root blushes a pale cherry pink, and hinona-zuke is treated as a taste of winter in Omi.
source_title: 滋賀県の郷土料理一覧（うちの郷土料理）

name_en: Yamada nezumi daikon — Shiga's short, mouse-shaped radish for crisp pickles
summary_ja: 滋賀県草津市の山田地区で受け継がれてきた短い白大根。長さ20cmほどで先が丸く、根の先端が尾のように伸びる姿がねずみに似ることから名がついたとされる。身が締まって水分が少なく、たくあんなどの漬物に向くという。
summary_en: A short white radish handed down in the Yamada district of Kusatsu, Shiga. About 20 cm long with a rounded tip and a thin tail of root, it is said to be named for its resemblance to a mouse (nezumi). The flesh is dense and low in moisture, which suits it to takuan and other pickles.

name_en: Kamo-nasu — Kyoto's round, dense heirloom eggplant from Kamigamo
summary_ja: 京都市北区の上賀茂・西賀茂一帯で育てられてきた大型の丸なす。直径10cm以上、300gほどになり、皮も身も締まって煮崩れしにくいという。油との相性がよく、田楽や揚げ出しにすると甘みが際立つとされる。
summary_en: A large round eggplant grown around Kamigamo and Nishigamo in Kyoto's Kita ward. It reaches over 10 cm across and around 300 g, with skin and flesh firm enough to hold together when cooked. It takes well to oil, and in dengaku (grilled with miso) or agedashi (fried, then sauced) its sweetness is said to come forward.
source_title: 賀茂なすの田楽 京都府 | うちの郷土料理

name_en: Kujo-negi — Kyoto's soft green leaf onion, sweetest after winter frost
summary_ja: 京都市南区の九条一帯で育てられてきた葉ねぎ。白い根元ではなく緑の葉を食べるねぎで、葉の内側にぬめりがあり、冬の霜にあたると甘みが増すとされる。薬味から鍋、肉豆腐まで京都の食卓に欠かせない野菜という。
summary_en: A leaf onion long grown around Kujo in Kyoto's Minami ward. Unlike the white-stemmed leeks of eastern Japan, it is the green leaves that are eaten; they hold a slippery sweetness inside and are said to turn sweeter after winter frost. From garnish to hot pots to nikudofu (beef and tofu), it is a fixture of Kyoto cooking.
source_title: 肉豆腐 京都府 | うちの郷土料理

name_en: Shogoin-kabu — Kyoto's giant sweet turnip behind senmai-zuke pickles
summary_ja: 京都市左京区の聖護院で育てられ始めたと伝わる大型の丸かぶ。直径15〜20cm、重さ2〜5kgにもなり、肉質はきめ細かく甘いとされる。薄く切って漬ける千枚漬けの原料として知られ、冬には鯛蕪のように炊いても食べるという。
summary_en: A very large round turnip said to have been first grown at Shogoin in Kyoto's Sakyo ward. It reaches 15 to 20 cm across and 2 to 5 kg, with fine-grained, sweet flesh. It is best known as the raw material for senmai-zuke, thin-sliced pickles, and in winter it is also simmered, as in taikabura with sea bream.
source_title: 鯛蕪／聖護院かぶと鯛の煮物 京都府 | うちの郷土料理

name_en: Manganji togarashi — Maizuru's big, thick-fleshed sweet pepper eaten whole
summary_ja: 京都府舞鶴市の万願寺地区で生まれたと伝わる大型のとうがらし。長さ15cm前後で肉厚、辛みがほとんどなく、焼くと甘みと青い香りが立つ。種ごと丸ごと焼いたり、じゃこと炊いたりして夏のおばんざいに使われるとされる。
summary_en: A large pepper said to have arisen in the Manganji district of Maizuru, Kyoto. Around 15 cm long and thick-fleshed, it carries almost no heat, and grilling brings out a sweetness and a green, grassy scent. It is cooked whole, seeds and all, or simmered with dried young sardines as a summer side dish.
source_title: 万願寺とうがらしとじゃこの炊いたん 京都府 | うちの郷土料理

name_en: Mibuna — Kyoto's smooth-leaved mustard green with a peppery bite
summary_ja: 京都市の壬生地区で水菜から分かれたと伝わる葉物野菜。水菜と違って葉に切れ込みがなく、へら形の葉が株から密に立ち上がる。ぴりっとした辛みとほのかな苦みがあり、からし和えや浅漬け、千枚漬けの添え物に使われるとされる。
summary_en: A leafy green said to have branched off from mizuna in the Mibu district of Kyoto. Unlike mizuna, its leaves have no serrated edges; smooth, spatula-shaped leaves rise densely from the crown. It has a peppery bite and a faint bitterness, and is used dressed with mustard, lightly pickled, or tucked beside senmai-zuke turnip pickles.
source_title: 壬生菜のからし和え 京都府 | うちの郷土料理

name_en: Tennoji kabura — Osaka's flat, sweet white turnip that grows half above the soil
summary_ja: 大阪市の天王寺あたりで古くから作られてきたと伝わる白かぶ。肩が平たく、根の半分ほどが土の上に出て育つ。肉質は締まって甘みが強く、生でも煮ても食べられ、なにわの伝統野菜として大阪府が位置づけている。
summary_en: A white turnip said to have long been grown around Tennoji in Osaka city. Its shoulders are flat and about half the root rises above the soil as it grows. The flesh is dense and markedly sweet, good raw or simmered, and Osaka prefecture lists it among the traditional vegetables of Naniwa, the city's old name.

name_en: Senshu mizunasu — Osaka's juicy eggplant tender enough to eat raw
summary_ja: 大阪府南部の泉州地域で育てられてきた、水分の多いなす。皮が薄く、身が柔らかくてあくが少ないため、手で裂いてそのまま食べられるとされる。ぬか漬けや浅漬けにして冷やしたものが初夏の泉州の味と伝わる。
summary_en: A water-rich eggplant long grown in the Senshu region of southern Osaka. The skin is thin and the flesh so tender and low in astringency that it can be torn by hand and eaten as is. Chilled, after a day or two in rice-bran or a light salt pickle, it is the taste of early summer in Senshu.
source_title: じゃこごうこ 大阪府 | うちの郷土料理

name_en: Awajishima tamanegi — Awaji Island's soft, sweet onion eaten raw
summary_ja: 兵庫県の淡路島で育てられてきたたまねぎ。収穫後に小屋で吊るしてゆっくり乾かすのが習いで、辛みが抜けて甘みが際立つとされる。身が柔らかく、薄切りを水にさらさずに生で食べるのが島の食べ方と伝わる。
summary_en: An onion long grown on Awaji Island, Hyogo. The custom is to hang the harvest in open sheds to dry slowly, which is said to draw out the sharpness and leave the sweetness. The flesh is soft, and the island way is to eat thin slices raw, without soaking them in water first.
source_title: 南あわじ市公式サイト

name_en: Iwatsu negi — Tajima's winter leek eaten white stem to green tip, sweetened under snow
summary_ja: 兵庫県北部の朝来市岩津地区で育てられてきたねぎ。白い根元も青い葉もどちらも柔らかく食べられる中間型で、雪の下で甘みを増すとされる。11月下旬から3月までの冬だけ出回り、鍋や焼きねぎで味わうと伝わる。
summary_en: A negi — a Japanese leek — grown in the Iwatsu district of Asago in northern Hyogo. It is an in-between type whose white stem and green leaves are both tender enough to eat, and it is said to sweeten under the snow. Sold only in winter, from late November to March, it is eaten in hot pots or simply grilled.
